findings.note: False test comment + a documented refusal path with zero CLI coverage. cli_test.go:296 says "escalation over three failed forks of the parent lineage is refused with the human-only code", but the line under it asserts ERR_CHECKPOINT_NOT_FOUND for `advance --run <id> --from nope` — a non-existent checkpoint name on a run that has been forked exactly once (attempt 1). Nothing in the test builds a three-deep failed lineage and no CLI test anywhere exercises ERR_RUN_ESCALATED, even though the CLI ships it in AgentPrompt (prompt.go:38) and maps it to exit 2 in exit2 (envelope.go:55). Proven by mutation: deleting the ERR_RUN_ESCALATED entry from exit2 — which would silently turn the human-only refusal into exit 1, contradicting the driver contract "exit 2: nothing was recorded … unless the code is a consent or escalation code" — leaves the entire repo suite green. Fix: either drive a real escalation through the CLI (machine/fork_test.go:599-623 shows how the lineage is built) or correct the comment and add the exit-mapping row to the exitFor table.

Spec 5 §8 explicitly lists "the `--repair` + pre-flight → exit 1 case" as a required CLI-suite row, and spec 5 §3 lists "ERR_RUN_NOT_FOUND from --repair at offset 0 (bytes moved)" as an exit-1 row; both are asserted only against the pure helper.

findings.note: A test whose failure message asserts a mapping the code does not have. cli_test.go:623-631 makes Deps.Rand fail and asserts a panic, with the message "rand failure panics into ERR_INTERNAL". The panic is never turned into ERR_INTERNAL: wiring.go:167-172 panics with errs.E(CodeInternal, …) and there is no recover() anywhere in non-test code in this repository (grep 'recover()' over all non-test .go files: zero hits), and cmd/metareview/main.go:100 calls fsmcli.Run directly inside os.Exit. So this path produces a Go stack trace on stderr and NOTHING on stdout — no envelope, no `code`, no mapped exit — which contradicts spec 5 §8 ("`Rand` failure → `ERR_INTERNAL`") and spec 5 §136 ("One JSON object on stdout for every subcommand except --agent-prompt"). Practical impact is low (crypto/rand.Read does not return errors in modern Go, so the seam exists only for this test), so the cheapest correct fix may be a recover-to-envelope in Run, or correcting the spec row and the test message — but as written the test enshrines behaviour the spec forbids while claiming the opposite.

findings.note: The mock-taint integrity signal is unverified in the CLI despite the package's 100% statement coverage. `mock` in every envelope (envelope.go:166) and in the status line (run.go:980) is `s.Mock != "" || s.MockTainted`; MockTainted is set by run/fold.go:89 when a product run (Mock == "") ingests a mock-stamped event — precisely the "a mock: true FSM row never satisfies a gate" guarantee the driver relies on. cli_test.go only ever exercises runs that are mock from init (mockInit) or pure product runs, never a tainted one, so dropping the `|| s.MockTainted` term at either CLI site survives the suite; the identical term in record.go:88 IS killed by internal/fsm/record tests. A refactor of viewKeys could therefore report mock:false to the driving agent for a run whose evidence is mock-contaminated while runs.jsonl still says mock:true, with no test noticing. Add one row that folds a mock-stamped event into a product run and asserts env["mock"] == true and the "  mock" status suffix.

(a) cli_test.go:275 "the child passed, the parent failed" — the check is only substring containment of the child id, "\"verdict\":\"PASS\"" and "\"mock\":true"; the parent row is never inspected (it is in fact NEEDS_REVISION, confirmed by dumping runs.jsonl), and the PASS substring would also match PASS_ADVISORY. findings.note: Two brittleness nits in the harness, neither currently failing. (1) harness.run (cli_test.go:108) indexes args[0] inside the JSON guard; `h.mustErr(CodeUsage, 2)` at line 164 calls it with zero args, so a change that made the no-arg path print non-JSON would turn a clean assertion failure into an index-out-of-range panic. Guard with len(args) > 0. (2) The empty-repository loop at cli_test.go:731-735 asserts only `code != 2`, so a future typo in one of the seven arg vectors would still pass as ERR_USAGE instead of the intended ERR_NO_RUNS/ERR_RUN_NOT_FOUND (I dumped the actual codes: three are ERR_NO_RUNS, four ERR_RUN_NOT_FOUND — all currently correct). Asserting the code, not just the exit, would pin the claim in the comment.
